claim: The constructor now wraps every analyzer report in `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`. That silently drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of the compilation, not just the ones the crash fix needed. Example: a `[MessagePackObject]` type declared in the compiling project that inherits a public, unattributed member from a referenced (non-MessagePackObject) base type. MsgPack004 then gets a null/None location and is discarded. The defining assembly never analyses that base type, so nobody reports the problem. The new README/MsgPack004 docs claim such problems are 'reported by the assembly that defines it', which is false here. The requirement asks only that these paths not crash, not that their diagnostics be suppressed.

In app declare `[MessagePackObject] public class Derived : Base { [Key(0)] public int Y { get; set; } }`. Run the analyzers via compilation.WithAnalyzers and assert that some MsgPack004 diagnostic is reported for Derived.X. On head no MsgPack004 is produced at all.

claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not an in-source location of this compilation, which includes Location.None. Previously such diagnostics were reported. Diagnostics created with a null or None location, such as MsgPack004 for a type whose inherited member comes from a referenced assembly, or diagnostics built from GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation helpers that return null, are now silently suppressed. The same applies to locations in another compilation's syntax tree, for example partial declarations or base types from a project reference with source. Users who relied on these warnings or errors will stop seeing them. That is a behaviour change beyond the crash fix, although it may be an acceptable one.
